newsitem.title: USA: Argentina reduced in Salomon LatAm portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Argentina reduced in Salomon LatAm portfolio.

text.p: Salomon Brothers analyst John Mullin has reduced Argentina to underweight from overweight in his model portfolio of Latin American stocks.
"On Jan 24, we reduced our overweight position in Argentina from three to 0.7 percent, following the market's 30 percent climb between August 1996 and January 1997," he wrote in an April 7 report.
"Since January, the market is up more than 10 percent. We now recommend moving to a 1.7 percent underweight position."
He recommended shifting assets to Chile and Panama. He trimmed his underweight position in the Chilean market to 1.7 percent from 3.1 percent.
The positions are based on a neutral benchmark which shifts with performances of markets and stock prices.

Mullin said the reasons for Argentina's reduction included the market's strength, the prospect of more U.S. interest rate rises and the possibility that major trading partner Brazil could move to limit imports.

"We recommend that investors lighten their Argentine exposure by moving from overweight to underweight in the banking sector ... and by moving to even greater underweight positions in holding companies."
Mullin also recommended that investors move from overweight to underweight in electric utilities, steel and cement and construction stocks.
